name: Measurement of the solar neutrino capture rate with gallium metal
title: Measurement of the solar neutrino capture rate with gallium metal

claim.quote: Measurement of the solar neutrino capture rate with gallium metal

summary.plain: SAGE measured how often the Sun's lowest-energy neutrinos struck its gallium target between 1990 and 1997, finding only about half the rate solar theory predicted — part of the long-standing 'solar neutrino problem'.
summary.technical: Solar neutrino capture rate on gallium, January 1990-December 1997, measured at 67.2 (+7.2/-7.0 stat) (+3.5/-3.0 syst) SNU, about half the Standard Solar Model prediction of 129 SNU.

why_it_matters.value: One of the gallium experiments (with GALLEX/GNO) confirming the solar neutrino deficit extended down to the lowest-energy pp neutrinos, later explained by neutrino oscillation.
why_it_matters.quote: This represents only about half of the predicted Standard Solar Model rate of 129 SNU.

key_value.note: SNU (solar neutrino unit) is not itself one of the atlas's recognised dimensions; recorded here with dimension `count` and unit "" as the closest available representation, with the true unit given in `display`.

key_value_text.value: 67.2 (+7.2/-7.0 stat) (+3.5/-3.0 syst) SNU, ~half the Standard Solar Model's 129 SNU prediction
key_value_text.quote: 67.2 (+7.2-7.0) (+3.5-3.0) SNU ... only about half of the predicted Standard Solar Model rate of 129 SNU

significance.note: A rate measurement, not a discovery/observation/evidence claim with a single sigma; no significance figure applies.

notes: Wikipedia separately cites a later, full-dataset (through 2007) capture rate of 65.4 SNU; this result record covers only the 1999 paper's 1990-1997 dataset and its own 67.2 SNU figure, sourced directly from the paper itself rather than the later secondary figure.
